answers.answer: To use the incoming message, I type {chat.message} for the whole message, or {chat.message.noCommand} for the message without the command word. {chat.mention.user} gives the viewer's name with an @. For chat settings, I type {chat.settings.slow}, {chat.settings.followersOnly}, {chat.settings.subOnly} or {chat.settings.emoteOnly}. To keep a reply within the limit, I wrap the whole reply in {chat.fit:text}, or in {chat.fit:text|end} for my own end text. The page gives a full example: {chat.fit:{chat.mention.user} wants to know: {chat.message.noCommand}|(cut short)}.
answers.quote: To cut a reply to the limit instead, put the whole reply inside {chat.fit:text}. Other helpers inside it fill in first, then the result is cut.

answers.answer: I must know where I can type the helpers: in a command, an event response, a timer, a pipeline, a Discord notification or a webhook. They do not work in text that viewers write. The message helpers work fully in commands only. In other places they work only for some events, and a timer that has them does not save. The table at the top of 'The message behind the reply' says this.
answers.quote: You type them in the text of a command, an event response, a timer, a pipeline, a Discord notification or a webhook. A section says so when its helpers work in fewer places.

answers.answer: Success: the helper is replaced by its value, such as back in five or @ViewerOne. Failure: the helper text shows in chat as I typed it, with its braces. For the fit helpers, a text that fits stays whole. A cut text ends in a space and … or a space and my own end text. {chat.fit:text} can cut in the middle of a word. {chat.fit.words:text} cuts before the word.
answers.quote: When a helper has nothing to read, such as a message helper in a Stream goes live post or in a pipeline that a timer starts, it prints exactly as you typed it, braces and all.

answers.answer: In a command, I can read the message with {chat.message.noCommand} or check its size with {chat.message.length}. Then I wrap the whole reply in {chat.fit:...|end}. The helpers inside fill in first, then the result is cut. The limit is 500 characters on Twitch and Kick and 200 on YouTube, and it comes from the platform of the person who started the reply. The end text counts toward the limit, so a long end text leaves less room for the message. A pipe that the viewer types in the message is plain text and does not split the inputs.
answers.quote: The ending counts toward the limit, either the space and … or the space and your own end text, so a long end text leaves less room.
